sub_answers.text: In 2014 North Hobart Football Club Inc. changed from an incorporated body to a company limited with 100% ownership of the Hobart City Football Club [d8767658s0p0]. The Hobart City Demons became the trading name of North Hobart Football Club Ltd following that change in 2014 [d8767658s0p0]. On October 9, 2017 paying members voted 371-118 in favour of returning the playing name of the club to the North Hobart identity for the 2018 season and beyond [d8767658s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What competitive declines, relegations, or periods of poor performance has the club endured and what reasons were given?
sub_answers.text: The club left the Tasmanian Football League in 2001 and joined the Southern Football League at that time [d8767658s0p0]. North Hobart was invited into the statewide league in 2009 and remained there until 2013 [d8767658s0p0]. After the 2013 season its position in the league was effectively filled by the Hobart City Football Club, and North Hobart later returned to the Tasmanian State League in 2018 [d8767658s0p0]. Following the cessation of the TSL in 2024 the club rejoined the Southern Football League in 2025 [d8767658s0p0].

sub_answers.text: The club competed in the Tasmanian Football League from the early 1900s until 2001 [d8767658s0p0]. The club joined the Southern Football League in 2001 and later was invited into the statewide Tasmanian league in 2009, where it remained until 2013 [d8767658s0p0]. After 2013 its position in the statewide league was effectively filled by the Hobart City Football Club, and in 2014 North Hobart reorganized as a company limited that held 100% ownership of Hobart City Football Club with Hobart City Demons as its trading name [d8767658s0p0]. North Hobart returned to the Tasmanian State League in 2018, and following the cessation of the TSL in 2024 the club rejoined the Southern Football League in 2025; in 2017 paying members voted to restore the North Hobart playing name for the 2018 season and beyond [d8767658s0p0].
